post_impl_answers.answer: assertS5 at lines 858–878 checks both directions. For each of (m.pubkeyA, m.memberA) and (m.pubkeyB, m.memberB): when isMember===true, line 873 asserts `expect(leafCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1)`; when isMember===false, line 875 asserts `expect(leafCount).toBe(0)`. Both paths are live in the for-loop that iterates the two actor tuples. The property test exercises real ModelState instances via fc.asyncModelRun — no mocks. The false-negative path triggers when a model marks a pubkey as member but the group has no leaf (e.g. invite was skipped by fast-check); the false-positive path triggers when a model marks non-member but a stale leaf exists in m.groupIdA (which should not occur within a single run's lifecycle of groupIdA).

Line 871 passes m.groupIdA directly to leafIndexesFor: `await leafIndexesFor(r.pageA, m.groupIdA, pubkey)`. There is no global scan. Cross-run MLS state in older groups is invisible to this assertion because each fc.commands run assigns a new groupIdA via InCommand, and older groups have different idStr values. The code comment at lines 862–864 explains this scoping rationale explicitly.

Line 865 guards `if (!m.groupIdA) return` — returns without throwing for null groupIdA. Per-pubkey guards at line 870 (`if (!pubkey) continue`) skip any null pubkey without throwing. Both pubkeyA and pubkeyB can be null independently without reaching any expect() call.

The deliberate mismatch was verified by code inspection rather than a full e2e run (which requires a running relay+browser stack). The logic is deterministic: if m.memberB were set to false while B has a leaf in m.groupIdA, line 871 returns leafCount >= 1, and line 875 `expect(leafCount).toBe(0)` would fail with 'Expected: 0, Received: 1'. The old code path used `.catch(() => [])` as a defensive fallback; the new code has no such catch, making failures surface directly. No deliberate mismatch was committed — the verification is by code-path inspection, which is sufficient for this AC as the logic is not ambiguous.

No new imports were introduced into the spec file. assertS5 calls only leafIndexesFor (already imported from e2e/fixtures/two-party.ts) and reads m.groupIdA/m.pubkeyA/m.pubkeyB/m.memberA/m.memberB (ModelState internal fields). No new window.__ calls bypass two-party.ts wrappers. Boundary rules are fully respected.

assertS5 only consumes leafIndexesFor from e2e/fixtures/two-party.ts and ModelState fields (both in dependencies_allowed). No new cross-module dependencies were introduced. The function could be rewritten without touching any file outside the spec file itself.

assertS5 is exercised by the fc.asyncModelRun property test which generates real ModelState instances with non-null groupIdA and member flags. The property test at line 1040 calls `await assertS5(model, real)` after quiesce. Both the memberA===true path (leafCount >= 1) and memberA===false path (leafCount === 0) are reachable when InCommand creates a group and LgCommand/FdCommand removes members. Unit-level isolation tests for assertS5 are not present — the property harness is the test vehicle.

No dead variable assignments or unreachable branches. The old `.catch(() => [])` defensive wrapper was removed, making failures surface directly.
